text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0023"
description = "`RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled` returning true means this handle names the profile's digest algorithm and its value IS the labeled digest of those bytes under that role's label."
justification = """
The replacement for ASM-0022, and deliberately much narrower: it constrains one three-line
comparator instead of leaving a twenty-line role-checking function meaningless.

What it does NOT assume is the important half. The digest is an UNINTERPRETED function of
`(label, bytes)` — nothing about SHA-256 is claimed, not collision resistance, not preimage
resistance, not even injectivity. Only functionality: the same label over the same bytes
gives the same value.

That is exactly enough to prove the binding DISCIPLINE — that each handle is checked under
its own required role label — and deliberately not enough to prove role SEPARATION, which
would need `label_a != label_b ==> digest(label_a, x) != digest(label_b, y)`. That is a
domain-separation property of the construction, it lives at
`boundary.crypto_primitives`, and no wording here should let it be read as proved.

The algorithm clause is a plain equality against the profile's single digest algorithm
identifier; it is trusted with the rest of the comparator.
"""
scope = ["unit://http_profile.continuation_binding", "boundary://boundary.unmodelled_own_behaviour"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "ADR-MCPRE-059 WP3"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to `RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled` or to its trusted Verus specification."
premise_class = "review-obligation"
discharging_event = { kind = "owner-event", statement = "`RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled` is proved, with the labeled digest left uninterpreted, to satisfy its comparator contract: a true answer implies the handle names the profile's digest algorithm and its digest value equals labeled_digest(label, bytes). No property of the digest construction is claimed." }
affected_contracts = ["contract://http_profile/block/continuation_verify"]
sites = [
  "mcp-re-http-profile/src/evidence/digest.rs#RequestEvidenceDigest::matches_labeled",
]
tool_specific_mechanism = "verus:external_body"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0079"
description = "`Instant` is monotonic and advances at true rate while the process runs."
justification = """
A reload is due a cadence after the last one, measured on `std::time::Instant`; a cached key's
authority ends at its first-caching reading of the cache's clock plus the window `T` (THM-0097),
and that clock is `Instant`-elapsed seconds plus the highest wall-minus-monotonic offset seen, so
it advances at least as fast as `Instant` and a wall-clock step can only shorten `T`. Those are
DURATIONS, which is why they are not read off the wall clock — and a duration means something only
if the monotonic clock never goes back and advances at the rate time does. A clock that stalls keeps a cached answer authoritative past
`T`; that is the failure that matters here.

It is not a wall-clock premise and is not implied by one: a monotonic clock is trusted to
advance, not to agree with any peer.

It stops being acceptable if the reload cadence is measured on anything but the monotonic clock, or
if the cache's clock is built on anything that can advance slower than it.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://proxy.trust_resolution_window",
  "unit://proxy.trust_reload_cadence",
  "unit://proxy.admission_currency_gate",
  "boundary://boundary.monotonic_clock",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 RERE-RATIFICATION §4b P-4 (Ruling 40 step 4)"
review_requirement = "Owner review if a trust-plane window or cadence is measured on anything but `Instant`."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The host operating system's monotonic clock, across `std::time::Instant::now()`: successive
readings never decrease, and their differences track elapsed real time while the process runs.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0083"
description = "When `serde_json::from_slice` succeeds on a byte string into a `Value`, the byte string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and for a text with no duplicate object member name the returned `Value` holds the object, array and scalar values that text encodes. When `serde_json::from_slice` succeeds on a byte string into the trust document's `Vec<RawEntry>` (`mcp-re-proxy/src/trust_document.rs`), the byte string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and each named field of each `RawEntry` (`signer`, `key_id`, `public_key`, `slots`) holds the JSON member value from which it was deserialized."
justification = """
THM-0083 refuses a body unless it is a legal JSON-RPC 2.0 request, and establishes the
outstanding id from that one validation. Every clause after the first reads the body through
`serde_json::from_slice::<Value>`. The FIRST clause is this project's and is not part of this
premise: `reject_unrepresentable_json` refuses a duplicate member name, on the decoded form
`serde_json` keys on, before `serde_json` is asked anything — because `serde_json` resolves a
duplicate to one winner. What remains trusted is one direction only: when the parse succeeds,
the body was a JSON text, and for a text with no duplicate the `Value` returned represents the
objects, arrays and scalars the text encodes. It is not trusted that every RFC 8259 text is
accepted: a refusal of a legal text is a refusal, which the envelope's clauses treat as one.

The operator's trust document is read through the typed form, `serde_json::from_slice` into
`Vec<RawEntry>` (THM-0098), and only that one type: it relies on the same soundness fact, together
with fidelity for that representation. A document the parse accepts is a JSON text, and the
strings and values placed in `signer`, `key_id`, `public_key` and `slots` are the ones the text
wrote for those members, which is what binds each key id to the signer that wrote it. Nothing is
claimed for any other type that derives `serde::Deserialize`. The refusals of a member written
twice, of an unknown member, of an unknown slot and of `slots` that is not an array are this
project's, pinned by its own tests
(`a_duplicated_member_is_refused_rather_than_read_last_wins`,
`an_unknown_member_is_refused_rather_than_ignored`, `an_unknown_slot_is_refused_rather_than_ignored`,
`slots_must_be_an_array_when_present`); they are not part of this premise.

It stops being acceptable if the request envelope is read through another parser, or if the
representability check stops running first.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://http_profile.request_envelope",
  "unit://proxy.trust_document_interpretation",
  "boundary://boundary.json_parser",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 RERE-RATIFICATION §4b P-8 (Ruling 40 step 4)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the JSON parsing dependency, or to the order in which the envelope's clauses are asked."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The `serde_json` crate, across `from_slice` on a byte string. Into a `Value`: when it succeeds, the byte
string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and for a text without duplicate member names the returned `Value`
holds the object, array and scalar values the text encodes. Into the trust document's
`Vec<RawEntry>`: when it succeeds, the byte string is an RFC 8259 JSON text, and each named field of
each `RawEntry` holds the JSON member value from which it was deserialized. It does not promise to
accept every RFC 8259 text, and nothing is claimed for any other type.
"""

tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0085"
description = "When MCP-RE decodes input through `ciborium` as a CBOR value, or through `coset` as a COSE_Sign1, and the decode succeeds, the decoded CBOR values correspond to the values the input bytes encode, and the decoded protected headers, unprotected headers, payload and signature are those the input bytes represent, with the protected and unprotected headers kept distinct. The `Sig_structure` that `coset` builds from such a decoded COSE_Sign1 for a signature check is the RFC 9052 section 4.4 encoding over the protected-header bytes exactly as received, and the external AAD and payload passed to it."
justification = """
THM-0041 reads a Signed Statement and a Receipt off the wire through `coset::CoseSign1` and
`ciborium`, and then reasons about what is in them: the algorithm and the claims it reads come
from the PROTECTED header, a receipt's position commitment comes from the protected header, and
its inclusion proof from the unprotected one. That the decoded structure is the one the bytes
encode, with the two headers not mixed, is the libraries' and nothing here establishes it.

The second sentence is for one conjunct: the Signed Statement's own COSE `Sig_structure` verified
under a key resolved for its issuer kid, and the same for the receipt's signature. MCP-RE does not
construct those signed bytes. `verify_cose_sign1_with_payload` hands `coset` a verifier callback and
`CoseSign1::verify_signature` / `verify_detached_signature` build the `Sig_structure` that is passed
to it. MCP-RE chooses the key, the algorithm check (`require_alg`) and, for a detached receipt, the
payload it re-derived.

Every refusal MCP-RE owns is NOT in this premise and is tested here: a non-empty or unknown `crit`,
an `iss` that is not the signing `kid`, a second occurrence of a CWT claim, trailing octets after
the statement's payload and after an inclusion proof, a repeated key in the `vdp` map, an unsupported
verifiable data structure, a leaf index outside the tree, and a root that is not a tree hash.

It stops being acceptable if SCITT evidence is decoded through another library, or if the signed
structure is ever built by this project instead of by `coset`.
"""
scope = [
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_statement_attribution",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_receipt_shape",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_derived_root",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_algorithm_agreement",
  "unit://http_profile.scitt_position_commitment",
  "boundary://boundary.cose_cbor",
]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 6 (owner ruling on the coset/ciborium premise)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the `coset` or `ciborium` dependency, or to how SCITT evidence is decoded or its signed structure is built."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The `ciborium` and `coset` crates, across a successful decode of CBOR input and of a COSE_Sign1,
and across the construction of the `Sig_structure` for a signature check from a decoded COSE_Sign1.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0086"
description = "`X509Certificate::verify_signature(None)` returns Ok only when the certificate signature verifies under the certificate's own subject public key."
justification = """
`credential_currency/x509_adapter` reports, for a certificate, whether it is self-signed: its
issuer `Name` encoding equals its subject `Name` encoding AND `verify_signature(None)` is Ok.
`evaluation` exempts a certificate reported self-signed from the validity-window check, so a
key-rollover intermediate (one that shares its name with its own issuer but is signed by another
key) is held to its window as path building holds it (THM-0032). Whether the exemption applies to
a given certificate therefore depends on `verify_signature(None)` answering Ok only for a signature
made under the certificate's own subject public key; the library's signature check is the
library's, and nothing here establishes it.

What stays this project's and is tested here: the comparison of the two `Name` encodings, the
conjunction of that comparison with the signature check, the exemption itself, and that the
validity window still applies to every certificate not reported self-signed
(`a_self_issued_certificate_is_self_signed_only_under_its_own_key`). This premise says nothing
about certificate trust, path validity, issuer selection or X.509 in general.

It stops being acceptable if the adapter checks a certificate's signature through another call,
or passes a key to `verify_signature` instead of `None`.
"""
scope = ["unit://proxy.credential_currency", "boundary://boundary.x509"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 7 (owner ruling on THM-0032)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the credential-currency X.509 adapter, to its parser dependency, or to how a certificate is reported self-signed."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The pinned `x509_parser` crate, across `X509Certificate::verify_signature(None)`: it returns Ok
only when the certificate's signature verifies under the certificate's own subject public key.
"""

tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0087"
description = "When `napi` invokes an exported `#[napi]` function of the TypeScript native binding, each `Buffer`, string, number and array argument arrives as the JavaScript caller passed it, and the object the function returns, or the error it raises, reaches the caller with each member and message as the function produced it, a member left `None` arriving absent."
justification = """
THM-0095 says what an application is handed, and the application receives it through `napi`:
the request bytes the exchange transmitted go in as a `Buffer`, the caller's trust inputs go in as
strings, numbers and arrays, and the verdict comes back as an object. The binding does everything
it owns before and after that layer: it passes the received bytes to the audited core unchanged,
builds the anchor and policy from the received values, and fills `VerifyResultJs` field for field
with an execution member the receipt did not state left `None`. That the bytes it received are the
bytes the caller passed, and that the object it built is the object the caller reads, is `napi`'s.

What stays this project's and is tested here: the refusal of an empty issuer identity, the
refusal of a time that is not whole seconds, the judgement of a retired root at the caller's
`now`, and the projection (`an_absent_execution_member_stays_absent_in_the_projection`,
`a_rejection_is_not_reported_as_a_success`). This premise says nothing about the Node runtime,
about `napi` correctness in general, or about what the TypeScript layer does with the object.

It stops being acceptable if the binding converts a value itself before handing it to the core, or
returns a type whose conversion this premise does not cover.
"""
scope = ["unit://sdk_typescript.native_binding", "boundary://boundary.napi_marshalling"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 7 (owner ruling on native marshalling)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the napi dependency, or to a type the binding takes or returns across the N-API boundary."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The pinned `napi` and `napi-derive` crates, across an exported `#[napi]` function: the `Buffer`,
string, number and array arguments arrive as passed, and the returned object or raised error
reaches the caller as produced, a member left `None` arriving absent.
"""
affected_contracts = []
tool_specific_mechanism = "foreign-dependency"

text:
[[assumption]]
id = "ASM-0088"
description = "When `pyo3` invokes a `#[pyfunction]` of the Python native binding, each `bytes`, `str`, `int` and `list` argument arrives as the Python caller passed it, or the call is refused before the function runs, and the `#[pyclass]` value the function returns, or the exception it raises, reaches the caller with each field and message as the function produced it, a field left `None` arriving as `None`."
justification = """
THM-0094 says what an application is handed, and the application receives it through `pyo3`: the
request bytes the exchange transmitted go in as `bytes`, the caller's trust inputs go in as `str`,
`int` and `list`, and the verdict comes back as a `PyVerifyResult`. The binding does everything it
owns before and after that layer: it passes the received bytes to the audited core unchanged,
builds the anchor and policy from the received values, and fills the result field for field with an
execution member the receipt did not state left `None`. That the bytes it received are the bytes
the caller passed, and that the object it built is the object the caller reads, is `pyo3`'s. A
value that does not fit its Rust parameter (an `int` beyond `i64`) is refused by `pyo3` before the
function runs; the premise relies on that refusal and on nothing converting the value instead.

What stays this project's and is tested here: the refusal of an empty issuer identity, the
judgement of a retired root at the caller's `now`, and the projection
(`an_absent_execution_member_stays_absent_in_the_projection`,
`a_rejection_is_not_reported_as_a_success`). This premise says nothing about the interpreter, about
`pyo3` correctness in general, or about what the Python layer does with the object.

It stops being acceptable if the binding converts a value itself before handing it to the core, or
returns a type whose conversion this premise does not cover.
"""
scope = ["unit://sdk_python.native_binding", "boundary://boundary.pyo3_marshalling"]
owner = "mats@sundvall.name"
introduced_by = "r12 step 7 (owner ruling on native marshalling)"
review_requirement = "Owner review on any change to the pyo3 dependency, or to a type the binding takes or returns across the PyO3 boundary."
premise_class = "external-boundary"
boundary_owner = """
The pinned `pyo3` crate, across a `#[pyfunction]`: the `bytes`, `str`, `int` and `list` arguments
arrive as passed or the call is refused, and the returned `#[pyclass]` value or raised exception
reaches the caller as produced, a field left `None` arriving as `None`.
"""
